messages:
Asha (Support): Heads-up - multiple customers reported streaming sessions terminating with a broken pipe and our billing pipeline counting them as 5xx. Customer A attached curl logs and says client sees EOF mid-stream, we see an upstream error in gateway logs. They want a root cause and a refund for the extra tokens counted.

Asha (Support): quick summary pasted from customer:
```
curl -v \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \ 
  -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' \ 
  -d @prompt.txt \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.10.10.10) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.example\n> Transfer-Encoding: chunked\n> \n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n< Transfer-Encoding: chunked\n< \ndata: {"delta":"..."}\n...then connection reset, client sees EOF, server logs: "write: broken pipe"
```

Asha (Support): Customer also attached gateway log snippet: `upstream write failed: connection reset by peer, client: 54.54.54.54, server: api.redwood.example, request: "POST /v1/stream"` and our metering shows this event counted as an upstream 5xx.

Devin (Eng-runtime): Thanks, Asha. First pass: need full request/response capture (headers + wire). Can you get a HAR or tcpdump from customer? Also paste the gateway logs for the same timestamp range (nginx/proxy logs + our runtime stdout).

Devin (Eng-runtime): Possible causes: client dropped connection (e.g., mobile app backgrounded), our gateway tried to push more chunk data after client close -> EPIPE/ECONNRESET; gateway currently maps upstream write errors to 502/5xx for metrics which might be inflating 5xx. We should treat client disconnects as 499-like and exclude from billing.

Li (SRE): I pulled a few correlated logs from the gateway for one of the accounts. Pattern: long-lived stream, then idle for ~32s, gateway logs `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)` then shortly after `write failed: broken pipe`. Stack: gateway -> runtime -> model worker. Idle timeout on the gateway is 30s (proxy_read_timeout). If the runtime flushes partial data after the client closed, gateway records upstream write error.

Li (SRE): Repro plan: 1) run a local client that opens a chunked POST, reads first chunk(s), then force-close socket without completing; 2) observe gateway and runtime behavior; 3) tcpdump to confirm which side sends FIN/RST.

Eli (Support): I have a repro script from the customer that mimics their Node client. Pasting trimmed version:
```
const net = require('net');
const req = net.connect({ host: 'api.redwood.example', port: 443 }, () => {
  // TLS + http framing omitted for brevity
  req.write("POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.example\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n4\r\ndata\r\n0\r\n\r\n");
  setTimeout(() => req.destroy(), 15000); // client kills connection mid-stream
});
```

Eli (Support): When we run that through our staging gateway, we see the runtime attempt to send another chunk, gateway logs write error, and the request shows as a 502 in our metrics backend.

Devin (Eng-runtime): Ok that's consistent. Two problems to solve: 1) Customer UX / root cause - why did runtime try to write after client closed? Maybe runtime flush policy/heartbeat. 2) Metric/classification - we should not count ECONNRESET caused by client closure as a service 5xx for billing or incident alerts.

Devin (Eng-runtime): Quick mitigations: - Change metrics mapping so ECONNRESET/EPIPE are recorded as client disconnect (499) when the gateway observed a client FIN before the upstream write. - Add a runtime guard: if write returns EPIPE, short-circuit rest of processing and don't produce further token accounting.

Li (SRE): I can whip up a small mapping patch in the gateway configpath to map these failures to 499 semantics for alerting/billing. Example pseudo-patch (not final):
```
# gateway: when upstream write fails with ECONNRESET/EPIPE
if (upstream_write_errno in [ECONNRESET, EPIPE] && client_closed_seen) {
  record_metric('client_disconnect', 1)
  return 499
} else {
  record_metric('upstream_error', 1)
  return 502
}
```

Li (SRE): Also bumping proxy_read_timeout to 60s on a canary to reduce false timed-out writes while we investigate.

Asha (Support): Customer is asking for a short-term refund and to know what we will change. Can legal/billing/ops prepare pro-rate and manual credit flow if we identify misbilling?

Eli (Support): I'll open an internal billing ticket and flag affected accounts. Need list of request ids for backfill. Devin, can runtime expose request-id in the final metric even on write failure? Right now token accounting is done incrementally and may have double-counted when write retried.

Devin (Eng-runtime): We'll add a per-request marker in the trace that notes whether any downstream write error occurred and a final accounting state (committed/aborted). That will let billing backfill. I will add a small endpoint to export request-ids with aborted=true for the last 48h.

Li (SRE): Action items I'm taking now:
- Deploy canary change to gateway mapping (499 behavior) to staging -> canary in prod for 10% traffic.
- Increase proxy_read_timeout to 60s on canary.
- Collect tcpdumps from reproduced runs and customer-provided pcap.

Devin (Eng-runtime): Action items from runtime side:
- Add guard so after EPIPE/ECONNRESET further token accounting stops and we mark request aborted.
- Expose aborted request list endpoint for billing.
- Add unit test that simulates client socket destroy mid-stream and verifies no extra accounting.

Eli (Support): I'll coordinate with customer, get pcap and curl -v output, and create the billing ticket with placeholder refunds.

Asha (Support): One more ask: can we add a temporary dashboard that shows "streaming aborted by client" vs "upstream error" counts? We need to respond to customers quickly if they ask for justification.

Li (SRE): Yup, I'll add a quick grafana panel on the canary that splits metrics by our new mapping.

Asha (Support): Thanks everyone. Please post updates here. Priority: P1 for the affected enterprise customers.

deploy-bot: `canary/deploy/gateway-mapping -> succeeded (canary 10%)`

Li (SRE): Canary is live. Early signal shows 40% of previous "upstream_error" events are now mapped to "client_disconnect" on canary traffic. This will reduce 5xx noise and billing exposure.

Devin (Eng-runtime): I've pushed a small runtime fix to stop accounting after write error; staging tests pass. Will ship to canary in 30m.

Eli (Support): Customer confirmed they can reproduce with our repro and will send pcap. I'll post it here when received. :thumbsup:

Asha (Support): Closing loop: after canary validation we'll backfill billing for impacted request-ids and reach out to each account with details. We'll keep this thread open until refunds are processed.
